architecture.voidVOID
# Compiled from source through the shared VOID frontend and LLVM backend.
func calculate(value: i32) -> i32:
    return value + 42

func entry(value: i32) -> i32:
    if value < 0:
        return 7
    return calculate(value)

LEARN VOID / DATA & BEHAVIOR

Generics

Reuse an operation while keeping its types.

Name a reusable operation

larger<t> compares two values and returns the larger one. The type parameter t connects both parameters to the result type, so the returned value keeps the chosen concrete type.

Let the call choose the type

In larger(score, 10), the compiler infers the integer type from the arguments. Input 5 returns 10; input 15 returns 15. The same operation can be instantiated for another compatible numeric type.

Keep requirements visible

The function relies on > being valid for its concrete type. Generic code is still type-checked; this example does not make arbitrary objects orderable. Interfaces provide a way to express required methods when a generic operation needs specific behavior.

LEARN VOID / CONCURRENCY

Async & await

Start work now. Await its result when you need it.

Async execution

This example uses the explicit async host adapter. Its source is checked by the compiler; it is not a synchronous CLI entry program.

Schedule, then await

Calling an async function queues work and returns an inferred task handle. In this example, both leaf calls are made before the first await. Each leaf returns its input plus one, so input 5 produces 6 + 7 = 13.

Cooperation has a clear boundary

await suspends the current async function until its task completes. Cooperative async work does not mean the tasks execute on multiple CPU cores. Await is supported inside async functions; async function values and async value-receiver methods are outside the current subset.

Execution support

This is complete source for the explicit async host adapter. The ordinary synchronous CLI entry adapter does not run async entry functions. Task handles have no public user-written type spelling. Public builds are not yet available.

LET THE CODE SPEAK

Small programs.
Real possibilities.

Choose a topic to explore complete VOID source, its expected result and the idea behind it. These are source examples; public compiler builds are not yet available.

NATIVE FOUNDATIONS

Native foundations

Pass an input to a small function and add 42. The program keeps the syntax easy to follow.

Read the guide →

FUNCTIONS & RECURSION

Functions & recursion

Calculate a factorial with one recursive function and a clear stopping point.

Read the guide →

READABLE LOOPS

Readable loops

Add the odd numbers from one through the limit using a single conditional loop.

Read the guide →

GROWABLE LISTS

Growable lists

Append a new score to a list, then add the scores together.

Read the guide →

VALUES & SHARED OBJECTS

Values & shared objects

Copy a point independently while two names share one counter.

Read the guide →

RESULTS & MATCHING

Results & matching

Return a recoverable result and handle each case explicitly.

Read the guide →

GENERICS

Generics

Write one typed operation that returns the larger of two values.

Read the guide →

PROPERTIES

Properties

Read a rectangle’s area through one computed property.

Read the guide →

FUNCTIONS & CLOSURES

Functions & closures

Let a function carry the state it needs.

Read the guide →

EVENTS

Events

Send a sensor reading to a display with one event subscription.

Read the guide →

SCOPED CLEANUP

Scoped cleanup

Use a scope to own cleanup of a small in-memory workspace.

An in-memory teaching model of scope ownership; no external file or native-resource API is assumed.

Read the guide →

ASYNC & AWAIT

Async & await

Start work now. Await its result when you need it.

Requires the explicit async host adapter; the ordinary synchronous CLI entry adapter does not execute this program.

Read the guide →

TASK GROUPS

Task groups

Schedule two updates and let the task group wait for both before reading the total.

Requires the explicit async host adapter; the ordinary synchronous CLI entry adapter does not execute this program.

Read the guide →

PARALLEL WORKERS

Parallel workers

Compute two squares independently on native workers and add their results.

Requires the explicit async host adapter; the ordinary synchronous CLI entry adapter does not execute this program.

Read the guide →

MODULES & IMPORTS

Modules & imports

Organize a program into small source files.

This example also needs math/calculator.void and helpers/numbers.void, kept in those relative paths.

Read the guide →
